# Evaluation report

*Generated by `jobintel bench all` on 2026-11-22 from `reports/*.json`. Every number below comes from those files.*

## How to read this report

* **Labels.** No human has graded these results yet. Relevance grades and gold skills were written by the AI assistant that built the system, blind to system outputs, with written rubrics. That is a conflict of interest; the numbers are *indicative* and the tooling accepts human grades (they take precedence automatically).
* **Small samples.** 10 retrieval queries, 3 synthetic candidates, 20+12 annotated listings, 26 assistant questions. Confidence intervals are wide on purpose: they are honest.
* **No significance theatre.** Paired bootstrap p-values are reported for retrieval only, as a descriptive aid.

## 1. Retrieval: five systems

Corpus: frozen 2026-10-23 snapshot (191 listings); 10 queries; 187 graded (query, job) pairs, pooled from every system's top 10.

## 2. Skill extraction from listings

Gold skills written by the AI assistant that built the extractor (blind to its output, written rules), NOT human-verified; a 20-listing dev set and a 12-listing held-out test set are small, so read the numbers as indicative.

| set | listings | gold skills | precision | recall | F1 (micro) | in-vocabulary recall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| dev, before error analysis | 20 | 248 | 0.980 | 0.798 | 0.880 | 0.912 |
| dev, after fixes (optimistic) | 20 | 248 | 0.981 | 0.839 | 0.904 | 0.959 |
| held-out test (after fixes) | 12 | 105 | 0.914 | 0.705 | 0.796 | 0.871 |

On the test set 19% of the gold skills are outside the taxonomy (e.g. LLM evaluation, MCP, LangGraph, Adobe Analytics, Google Ads, Adobe Launch, Google Analytics, Google Tag Manager, Tealium, NoSQL, AI coding assistants, AI orches…): a dictionary extractor cannot find them, which is the main recall limit.

Sector heuristic on the test listings: accuracy 0.33 where it predicts, coverage 0.25 - too weak to rely on; the UI labels it an estimate.

## 3. Matching: ranking a candidate's eligible jobs

Grades: assistant-proposed (written by the AI that built the system, blind to its rankings), NOT human-verified; only 3 synthetic candidates, so fitted weights can easily over-fit - which is exactly what the leave-one-candidate-out protocol checks.

| ordering | mean nDCG@10 | cv_en_ml_engineer | cv_en_student_data_science | cv_fr_data_engineer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| retrieval order (RRF) | 0.665 | 0.416 | 0.676 | 0.903 |
| rule-based evidence level | 0.635 | 0.561 | 0.797 | 0.548 |
| observed score (default weights) | 0.646 | 0.564 | 0.829 | 0.545 |
| ranking score (default weights) | 0.661 | 0.572 | 0.804 | 0.606 |
| ranking score (weights fitted, leave-one-CV-out) | 0.637 | 0.590 | 0.841 | 0.480 |

**Conclusion.** Fitted weights reach nDCG@10 0.789 in-sample but 0.637 out-of-sample vs 0.661 for the documented default weights; the fit does not generalise, so the default weights are kept.

**Eliminatory constraints vs labels:** precision of exclusions 1.00 (21 excluded and labelled ineligible, 0 wrongly excluded), recall 0.72 (8 ineligible jobs kept - mostly constraints stated only in free text, e.g. 'freelance position', which the system treats as unknown).

## 4. Career assistant (RAG)

Automatic metrics on 26 hand-written questions (EN/FR) over 3 synthetic CVs and the live corpus; no human rating of answer quality. The verifier is also the faithfulness checker, so faithfulness measures agreement with its rules, not truth.

| mode | routing_accuracy | citation_validity | faithfulness | hallucination_rate | fallback_rate | answer_relevance | retrieval_relevance | forbidden_claims_in_final | latency_median_s | est_llm_tokens_per_question |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| deterministic | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.988 | 0.012 | 0.000 | 0.822 | 0.933 | 0 | 0.079 | 0 |
| llm-ollama | 1.000 | 0.985 | 0.721 | 0.279 | 0.192 | 0.846 | 0.920 | 0 | 8.303 | 691 |

*faithfulness / hallucination rate are measured on the sentences PROPOSED by the generator, before the verifier removes unsupported ones; what the user sees has passed the verifier. The verifier checks named entities, numbers, credentials and topical overlap - not the truth of qualitative statements.*

## Known biases and limits

* **Pool bias.** The original retrieval pool came from BM25, dense and hybrid; keyword and re-rank results were judged afterwards for the gaps (see judged@10).
* **Corpus.** Three job boards, data/AI titles only; Himalayas is remote-only and US-heavy; the frozen evaluation corpus is Arbeitnow only (Germany/Netherlands/France heavy). Results may not transfer to other markets.
* **Synthetic CVs.** Three invented candidates; real CVs have messier layouts (the parser is rule-based).
* **Same author.** System, labels and rubrics come from the same assistant: human review of `data/eval/proposals/*` is the next step (`jobintel label …` tools exist).
